name: Data-Analyst Agent With Code Execution and an Ops Agent With Allow-Listed CLI Commands
query: Two agents in Python. A `data_analyst` that writes and runs Python snippets against CSVs we hand it — ideally sandboxed. And an `ops_agent` that can run `gh` and `aws` CLI commands (it needs a GitHub token) to triage incidents — nothing else, and no arbitrary shell. What guardrails does the SDK give me, and where do the credentials go?
expected_behavior: Step 1: Consult references/agent-sdks.md §7 (`local_code_execution=True, allowed_languages=["python"], allowed_commands=["python3"]`; `code_execution=CodeExecutionConfig(executor=DockerCodeExecutor(image="python:3.12-slim"))` — also Jupyter / Serverless executors; `cli_commands=True, cli_allowed_commands=["gh", "aws"], credentials=["GH_TOKEN"]` or `cli_config=CliConfig(allowed_commands=[...], timeout=60, working_dir="/work", allow_shell=False)`), references/agents.md §4 (`cli_commands` / `cli_allowed_commands` / `cli_config`; `local_code_execution` / `allowed_languages` / `code_execution`; `credentials[]`), §5 (`cli` → server-side sandboxed `run_command` tool with an allow-list; `LocalCodeExecutor` / `DockerCodeExecutor` / `JupyterCodeExecutor` / `ServerlessCodeExecutor`), §8 secrets, references/optimization.md F2 (shell/code tools need allow-lists — `cliConfig` / `codeExecution` with empty allow-lists is CRITICAL), F5, F1.

Step 2: `coder = Agent(name="data_analyst", model="openai/gpt-4o-mini", instructions="Write and run Python to answer questions about the provided CSV.", local_code_execution=True, allowed_languages=["python"], allowed_commands=["python3"], max_turns=10)`; sandboxed variant: `Agent(name="data_analyst", ..., code_execution=CodeExecutionConfig(executor=DockerCodeExecutor(image="python:3.12-slim")), max_turns=10)` with `from conductor.ai.agents import CodeExecutionConfig, DockerCodeExecutor` — recommend Docker for untrusted snippets; mention Jupyter / Serverless executors exist.

Step 3: `ops = Agent(name="ops_agent", model="openai/gpt-4o-mini", instructions="Triage incidents using gh and aws.", cli_commands=True, cli_allowed_commands=["gh", "aws"], credentials=["GH_TOKEN"], max_turns=12)` or the explicit `cli_config=CliConfig(allowed_commands=["gh", "aws"], timeout=60, working_dir="/work", allow_shell=False)`; the agent gets a single sandboxed `run_command` tool restricted to the allow-list; `allow_shell=False` means no `sh -c`, pipes or arbitrary binaries.

Step 4: Guardrails (F2): allow-lists are mandatory — `allowed_languages` / `allowed_commands` / `cli_allowed_commands` empty is CRITICAL; for destructive verbs (`aws ... delete`, `gh repo delete`) add an input `RegexGuardrail(patterns=[...], mode=block, position=INPUT)`, narrow the allow-list, or cap with `max_calls`; consider `approval_required` on any separate write tool.

Step 5: Credentials (F5): `credentials=["GH_TOKEN"]` lists the NAME; the value is stored server-side (`CONDUCTOR_SECRET_GH_TOKEN` env on OSS, `/api/secrets` when writable, UI `/agentSecrets`, or Orkes) and injected at call time — never in `instructions`, `prompt` or code.

Step 6: Lifecycle under `if __name__ == "__main__":` — `runtime.run(...)`; `runtime.plan(...)` and check `requiredWorkers` (state that if it is non-empty a `runtime.serve(...)` process is needed — Rule 9 / F3); `runtime.deploy(coder, ops)` in CI. Never `conductor deploy`.
Step 7: Bounds (F1): `max_turns` on both agents; `timeout` in `CliConfig`; `maxDurationSeconds` + workflow timeout on any `AGENT` caller (`agentType: "conductor"`, `name`).
success_criteria: Offers `DockerCodeExecutor` as the sandboxed option (optionally mentioning Jupyter / Serverless executors)
States `allow_shell=False` (no arbitrary shell) and that allow-lists are required — empty allow-lists are CRITICAL under F2
`credentials=["GH_TOKEN"]` by NAME with the value in the server-side secret store; no token in `instructions` / prompt / code (F5)
Adds a further gate for destructive commands (input guardrail, narrower allow-list, `max_calls`, or `approval_required`) or explicitly calls out the F2 risk
Deploys with `runtime.deploy(...)` — never `conductor deploy` — and checks `plan()`'s `requiredWorkers` / states when `serve()` is needed
Any `AGENT` task uses `agentType: "conductor"` + `name` — never a framework name
